stories.title: Too Big to Fire: Jensen Huang’s Return to Nvidia
stories.take: The answer: Huang was reinstated because Trump intervened directly — Trump, Vance and the Justice Department assured the board Huang posed no national security risk and faced no criminal charges • Nvidia lost about $1.5 trillion in the week after the board said he would not return; the stock rose about 30% on his return • Reporters stress there is no evidence Huang knowingly committed crimes, but the relationship itself posed a risk — Rubio had written a memo on it • Ahead: closed-door congressional testimony, plus state and shareholder lawsuits Trump cannot block

stories.title: Trump's Push To Reinstate Huang, Market Reacts To Nvidia, Russia-Ukraine War Widening
stories.take: Huang is back as Nvidia CEO 11 days after resigning; Trump says he convinced the board, citing the stock plunge after the ouster • Nvidia rose more than 30% — just under $1 trillion in one day, the biggest one-day gain ever — and CoreWeave jumped 22% on Nvidia's backstop role • Rubio's memo warned about the relationship and Sen. Ricketts broke ranks; Huang testifies before the Senate in December • The Russia-Ukraine war is widening geographically — into Eastern and Northern Europe and the Mediterranean — even as the administration claims peace progress

stories.title: Nvidia’s ‘Key-Man Risk’ Is Bigger Than Ever
stories.take: Nvidia's key-man risk has only grown: Huang has 60 direct reports and apparently no chief compliance officer — 'too big to fire and too big to fail' • Three investigation tracks loom: Nvidia's internal probe, a DOJ investigation, and expected investigations from a Democratic Congress • Bipartisan backlash on Capitol Hill: a closed-door House interview and a public Senate Banking hearing in early December are still on • Also in the episode: the U.S. probes possible Iranian involvement in cyber attacks on as many as 50 energy tankers, and the Pentagon talks drone production with GM and Ford

stories.title: Unprecedented Corruption: How Jensen Huang Got His Job Back
stories.take: How he got his job back: Trump intervened directly and said he convinced the board; the White House rationale was 'we have to protect our geniuses,' and the board then voted unanimously to reinstate him • The hosts' verdict: political pressure overriding governance — corruption that moves the U.S. from rule of law to rule of man, bad for trust and markets despite the stock pop • Nvidia jumped more than 30% Monday after falling nearly 50% from its peak; the S&P 500 climbed nearly 5% • Not over: Huang is still expected to testify before Congress next week and Nvidia's independent investigation is ongoing

stories.title: The ‘Everywhere, All at Once’ Cybersecurity Crisis
stories.take: The recent outage cluster — an FAA ground stop, Microsoft Outlook, Apple iCloud and Chase — was not an attack: systems broke while being upgraded and hardened against attacks that are coming • Nicole Perlroth's core claim: AI now finds and exploits vulnerabilities at machine speed, putting everyone on 'the attacker's clock' and forcing faster, breakage-prone patching • The cost of a very good attack has collapsed while defense stays hard; incident-response firms are out of capacity and turning away breach victims • The new normal she expects: outages and attacks become routine as every actor — states and criminals alike — gains zero-day capability

stories.title: What Jensen Huang's Stunning Return Means for the AI Trade
stories.take: The answer: Huang's return sparked an epic relief rally — Nasdaq 100 up 6.9% — but it does not answer the AI trade's core questions on financing and revenue/ROI • Barclays' Alexander Altman flipped tactically bullish after a bombed-out washout, in a new high-vol regime (VIX 40 Friday, still 30) • The structural problems remain: data-center financing costs, overcapacity and unproven returns will still be there tomorrow • New wildcard: a possible 'White House put' — the administration is all-in on propping up the AI trade because AI has become the stock market

stories.title: Is Jensen Huang too big to fail?
stories.take: The answer: effectively yes — Huang was reinstated within a week of resigning, after the board reversed its own unanimous decision following Trump's call urging his return • Markets treated him as irreplaceable: Nvidia rose about 30%, adding roughly a trillion dollars in market cap in a day; the S&P 500 rose close to 5% • A petition drew over 10,000 Nvidia employees and over 100,000 shareholders, and executives including Elon Musk pushed for his return • The lift spread: a basket of debt-heavy neoclouds — firms Nvidia backstops, like CoreWeave — rose 18% in one day
